accepted.title: Deconstructive Oxygenation of Cyclic Amines by Copper-Catalyzed C(sp3)–C(sp3) Bond Cleavage
accepted.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed deconstructive oxygenation platform for the direct conversion of unstrained N-unsubstituted cyclic amines into versatile β-, γ-, and δ-aminoketones. The product diversity is achieved by adjusting the substituents at the β- or γ-position of cyclic amines that proceed through single or consecutive C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond cleavage, respectively. Following this method, we achieved skeletal modification of unstrained cyclic amines through ring contraction or atom replacement, leading to rapid structural diversification of cyclic amines. The synthetic utility of this method was further demonstrated by the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, fluoxetine, atomoxetine, and norfluoxetine. Control experiments indicated that, in the presence of the co-oxidant nitroxyl, the copper-catalyzed sequential dehydrogenative oxidation followed by single-electron transfer-induced aerobic oxygenative C–C bond cleavage was responsible for this effective transformation.

accepted.title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
accepted.abstract: ABSTRACT Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

accepted.title: Leveraging Cubenes to Access Highly Functionalized Fused Cubes
accepted.abstract: Abstract Since 1913, cubane has fascinated chemists owing to its remarkable structure. More recently, however, cubanes have emerged as attractive bioisosteres for aromatic rings. Although substituted derivatives are relatively common, ring-fused cubanes (a.k.a. “fused cubes”) are rare and can be difficult to access. Here, we report a strategy for the synthesis of fused cubes leveraging cubenes, unusual fleeting intermediates possessing hyperpyramidalized alkenes, in strain-promoted trapping reactions. Further, experimental and computational studies for the generation and reactivity of unsubstituted cubene and new substituted cubenes are disclosed. These studies not only push the limits of strained intermediate chemistry but also provide an entryway to highly functionalized fused cubes, including new three-dimensional hybrid structures and other unprecedented chemical space.

accepted.title: Photocatalytic tetrapeptides for enantioselective visible light-induced transformations
accepted.abstract: Abstract Research on enantioselective photocatalysis has so far been focused on molecular photocatalysts or large yet easily adaptable photoenzymes. However, both catalysis classes display deficiencies either due to their limited adaptability or their high molecular weight. Here we show that small peptides can bridge the gap between the currently used photocatalysts by combining structural flexibility and low molecular weight. We constructed a small peptide that displays a pyroglutamic acid at its N terminus for substrate recognition. At the C terminus, a thioxanthone-based amino acid was installed to harvest photons and to act catalytically by energy transfer. Two amino acids were sufficient to link the two components, resulting in a photocatalytically active tetrapeptide that was used both for photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. Our results demonstrate that small peptides with a molecular weight below 750 Da can act as efficient molecular catalysts for enantioselective photochemical transformations.

accepted.title: Scrambling-free synthesis of heteroleptic silylium ions by halide abstraction from halosilanes
accepted.abstract: Abstract Heteroleptic silylium ions with different substituents at the silicon atom are generally not accessible using established tools for producing such reactive intermediates because substituent exchange reactions occur in acidic media, leading to homoleptic silylium ions with three identical alkyl and aryl substituents, respectively. Here we report a broadly applicable route to heteroleptic silylium ions using halosilanes as silylium ion precursors, which are less prone to that scrambling process. While this deceptively simple method has failed so far owing to the lack of a suitable halide-abstracting agent, superhalophilic halogen-substituted silylium ions enable smooth halide abstraction from a diverse set of halosilanes at ambient temperature without substituent redistribution. Accordingly, this approach provides access to essentially any heteroleptic acyclic as well as cyclic silylium-ion motif from common halosilanes, including trialkyl-, dialkyl(aryl)-, alkyldiaryl- and triaryl-substituted congeners. Computational calculations reveal the mechanism of heteroleptic silylium-ion formation and the origin of the suppressed substituent-scrambling process.
